5. Input: the input parameters, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
6. Output: output value, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;

8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Class Diagram
```plantuml
@startuml

title trainingSchool Model

class Course {
    id : String
    documents : List<Document>
    sector : Sector
    sessions : List<Session>
    addDocument(doc : Document) : boolean
    addSession(date : LocalDate) : List<Session>
    cancelSession(date : LocalDate) : boolean
    removeDocument(doc : Document) : boolean
}
class Document {
    name : String
}
class Participant {
}
abstract class Person {
    id : String
}
class School {
    name : String
    courses : List<Course>
    sectors : List<Sector>
    addCourse(id : String) : boolean
    addSector(id : String) : Sector
    assignCourseToSector(courseId : String, sectorId : String) : boolean
}
class Sector {
    id : String
    courses : List<Course>
    addCourse(course : Course) : void
    removeCourse(course : Course) : void
}
class Session {
    date : LocalDate
    registeredParticipants : List<Participant>
    trainer : Trainer
    assignTrainer(t : Trainer, today : LocalDate) : boolean
    registerParticipant(p : Participant, today : LocalDate) : boolean
    replaceTrainer(newTrainer : Trainer, today : LocalDate) : boolean
}
class Trainer {
    contractor : boolean
}

Course --> "*" Document : documents
Course --> Sector : sector  'opposite: courses
Course *-- "*" Session : sessions
Participant --|> Person
School *-- "*" Course : courses
School *-- "*" Sector : sectors
Sector --> "*" Course : courses  'opposite: sector
Session --> "*" Participant : registeredParticipants
Session --> Trainer : trainer
Trainer --|> Person
@enduml
```

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Operation Specifications
Session::replaceTrainer
Summary: Replaces the currently assigned trainer with a new one. Strictly enforces replacement before the session date.
Algorithm: 
  1. If newTrainer is null, return false.
  2. If today >= this.date, return false (same-day or past operations disallowed).
  3. If this.trainer is null, return false (nothing to replace).
  4. Set this.trainer = newTrainer.
  5. Return true.
Related Features: trainer, date
Related Classes: Trainer, LocalDate
Input: newTrainer (Trainer): The replacement trainer object. today (LocalDate): Current system date. Format: Objects & yyyy-MM-dd. Value range: Non-null.
Output: boolean: true if replacement succeeded; false otherwise.
Pre-condition: newTrainer is not null. today is strictly earlier than this.date. Session currently has an assigned trainer.
Post-condition: this.trainer is updated to newTrainer. The previous trainer is unassigned.

Session::registerParticipant
Summary: Enrolls a participant in the session. Prevents duplicate registrations for the same participant.
Algorithm: 
  1. If p is null, return false.
  2. Check if p exists in this.registeredParticipants.
  3. If yes, return false.
  4. Append p to this.registeredParticipants.
  5. Return true.
Related Features: registeredParticipants
Related Classes: Participant, LocalDate
Input: p (Participant): The participant object to enroll. today (LocalDate): Current system date (reserved for future validation hooks). Format: Objects & yyyy-MM-dd. Value range: Non-null.
Output: boolean: true if enrollment succeeded; false if participant is null or already enrolled.
Pre-condition: p is not null. p is not already registered for this session.
Post-condition: p is added to this.registeredParticipants. No duplicate entries exist.

Session::assignTrainer
Summary: Assigns a trainer to lead this session. Strictly enforces that assignment occurs before the session date.
Algorithm: 
  1. If t is null, return false.
  2. If today >= this.date, return false (same-day or past operations disallowed).
  3. If this.trainer is already assigned, return false.
  4. Set this.trainer = t.
  5. Return true.
Related Features: trainer, date
Related Classes: Trainer, LocalDate
Input: t (Trainer): The trainer object to assign. today (LocalDate): Current system date. Format: yyyy-MM-dd. Value range: Non-null.
Output: boolean: true if trainer was successfully assigned; false otherwise.
Pre-condition: t is not null. today is strictly earlier than this.date. Session currently has no assigned trainer.
Post-condition: this.trainer is set to t. Assignment timestamp implicitly satisfies the pre-session deadline rule.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Operation Specifications
Session::replaceTrainer
Summary: Replaces the currently assigned trainer with a new one. Strictly enforces replacement before the session date.
Algorithm: 
  1. If newTrainer is null, return false.
  2. If today >= this.date, return false (same-day or past operations disallowed).
  3. If this.trainer is null, return false (nothing to replace).
  4. Set this.trainer = newTrainer.
  5. Return true.
Related Features: trainer, date
Related Classes: Trainer, LocalDate
Input: newTrainer (Trainer): The replacement trainer object. today (LocalDate): Current system date. Format: Objects & yyyy-MM-dd. Value range: Non-null.
Output: boolean: true if replacement succeeded; false otherwise.
Pre-condition: newTrainer is not null. today is strictly earlier than this.date. Session currently has an assigned trainer.
Post-condition: this.trainer is updated to newTrainer. The previous trainer is unassigned.

Session::registerParticipant
Summary: Enrolls a participant in the session. Prevents duplicate registrations for the same participant.
Algorithm: 
  1. If p is null, return false.
  2. Check if p exists in this.registeredParticipants.
  3. If yes, return false.
  4. Append p to this.registeredParticipants.
  5. Return true.
Related Features: registeredParticipants
Related Classes: Participant, LocalDate
Input: p (Participant): The participant object to enroll. today (LocalDate): Current system date (reserved for future validation hooks). Format: Objects & yyyy-MM-dd. Value range: Non-null.
Output: boolean: true if enrollment succeeded; false if participant is null or already enrolled.
Pre-condition: p is not null. p is not already registered for this session.
Post-condition: p is added to this.registeredParticipants. No duplicate entries exist.

Session::assignTrainer
Summary: Assigns a trainer to lead this session. Strictly enforces that assignment occurs before the session date.
Algorithm: 
  1. If t is null, return false.
  2. If today >= this.date, return false (same-day or past operations disallowed).
  3. If this.trainer is already assigned, return false.
  4. Set this.trainer = t.
  5. Return true.
Related Features: trainer, date
Related Classes: Trainer, LocalDate
Input: t (Trainer): The trainer object to assign. today (LocalDate): Current system date. Format: yyyy-MM-dd. Value range: Non-null.
Output: boolean: true if trainer was successfully assigned; false otherwise.
Pre-condition: t is not null. today is strictly earlier than this.date. Session currently has no assigned trainer.
Post-condition: this.trainer is set to t. Assignment timestamp implicitly satisfies the pre-session deadline rule.

  3. Return true.

Related Classes: Document

Output: boolean: true if the document was successfully added; false otherwise.

Post-condition: doc is present in this.documents list. The course now references the document.

Course::addSession
Summary: Schedules a new training session for the course on a specified date, enforcing a maximum of one session per course per day. Returns the updated session roster.
Algorithm: 
  1. If date is null, return this.sessions.
  2. Check if any existing session in this.sessions has date equal to input date.
  3. If a session already exists for this date, return this.sessions (no change).
  4. Else, instantiate new Session with session.date = input date.
  5. Add new Session to this.sessions.
  6. Return this.sessions.
Related Features: sessions
Related Classes: Session, LocalDate
Input: date (LocalDate): The date of the session. Format: yyyy-MM-dd. Value range: Valid calendar date.
Output: List<Session>: The complete, up-to-date list of sessions for this course after the operation.
Pre-condition: date is a valid, non-null LocalDate.
Post-condition: If no session existed for the date, a new session is created and added to this.sessions. Otherwise, this.sessions remains unchanged.

Summary: Detaches and deletes a referenced document from the course.
Algorithm: 
  1. If doc is null or doc is not contained in this.documents, return false.
  2. Remove doc from this.documents.
  3. Return true.
Related Features: documents
Related Classes: Document

  3. If session.registeredParticipants.size() > 0, return false.
  4. Else, remove session from this.sessions.
  5. Return true.

Related Classes: Session, Participant

Pre-condition: date is a valid, non-null LocalDate.
Post-condition: If successful, the session corresponding to date is removed from this.sessions. Otherwise, this.sessions is unchanged.

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Operation Specifications
School::assignCourseToSector
Summary: Assigns a course to a target sector. Ensures exclusive assignment by removing the course from any previously linked sector before linking to the new one.
Algorithm: 
  1. Locate course in this.courses by matching course.id with courseId. If not found, return false.
  2. Locate sector in this.sectors by matching sector.id with sectorId. If not found, return false.
  3. If course.sector is not null:
       a. Call course.sector.removeCourse(course).
       b. Set course.sector = null.
  4. Set course.sector = targetSector.
  5. Call targetSector.addCourse(course).
  6. Return true.
Related Features: courses, sectors, Course.sector, Sector.courses
Related Classes: Course, Sector
Input: courseId (String): ID of the course to assign. sectorId (String): ID of the target sector. Format: Strings. Value range: Non-null.
Output: boolean: true if assignment succeeded; false if IDs are invalid.
Pre-condition: Both courseId and sectorId correspond to existing entities in the school.
Post-condition: The specified course is exclusively bound to the specified sector. Any prior sector binding is severed and the course is added to the new sector's roster.

School::addCourse
Summary: Registers a new course in the school using a case-sensitive unique identifier.
Algorithm: 
  1. If id is null or empty, return false.
  2. Iterate over this.courses to check for case-sensitive match with id.
  3. If a match exists, return false.
  4. Else, instantiate new Course with course.id = id.
  5. Add new Course to this.courses.
  6. Return true.
Related Features: courses
Related Classes: Course, String
Input: id (String): The unique, case-sensitive identifier for the course. Format: Alphanumeric string. Value range: Non-null, non-empty.
Output: boolean: true if the course was successfully added; false if invalid or duplicate.
Pre-condition: id is non-null and non-empty.
Post-condition: If successful, a new course with the given id is stored in this.courses. Uniqueness constraint is preserved.

School::addSector
Summary: Creates a new sector with a unique identifier within the school's administrative structure.
Algorithm: 
  1. If id is null or empty, return null.
  2. Iterate over this.sectors to check for existing sector with matching id.
  3. If a match exists, return null.
  4. Else, instantiate new Sector with sector.id = id.
  5. Add new Sector to this.sectors.
  6. Return new Sector.
Related Features: sectors
Related Classes: Sector, String
Input: id (String): The unique identifier for the sector. Format: Alphanumeric string. Value range: Non-null, non-empty.
Output: Sector: The newly created sector object, or null if creation failed.
Pre-condition: id is non-null and non-empty.
Post-condition: If successful, a new sector with the given id is stored in this.sectors. Uniqueness constraint is preserved.

# Task
You will be given a **Requirement** and a **Class Diagram** in PlantUML. Your task is to annotate every operation listed in **Operations** with a specification.

An operation specification must describe the following sections about the operation:
1. Summary: the summary of functionality;
2. Algorithm: algorithm or pseudo code;
3. Related Features: a list of structural or behavior features within this class that shall be accessed;
4. Related Classes: a list of classes and data types defined in **Class Diagram** that shall be accessed, in the format of `Related Classes: ClsA, CLsB, ...` or `Related Classes: None`;
5. Input: the input parameters, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
6. Output: output value, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
7. Pre-condition: the condition that the system and the input must satisfy before the operation is executed;
8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

Finish this task by following the guidelines below.
1. Take the principle of modularization into account.
2. For each operation, determine its functional boundary based on the given requirement. Ensure high cohesion and low coupling.
3. If there is any unspecified details, such as undefined constants, rates, and ratios, then you must infer them.
4. Make sure that all requirements can be covered.

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

title trainingSchool Model

class Course {

}

    addCourse(id : String) : boolean
    addSector(id : String) : Sector
    assignCourseToSector(courseId : String, sectorId : String) : boolean
}
class Sector {
    id : String
    courses : List<Course>
    addCourse(course : Course) : void
    removeCourse(course : Course) : void
}
class Session {
    date : LocalDate
    registeredParticipants : List<Participant>
    trainer : Trainer
    assignTrainer(t : Trainer, today : LocalDate) : boolean
    registerParticipant(p : Participant, today : LocalDate) : boolean
    replaceTrainer(newTrainer : Trainer, today : LocalDate) : boolean
}
class Trainer {
    contractor : boolean
}

Course --> "*" Document : documents
Course --> Sector : sector  'opposite: courses

School *-- "*" Sector : sectors
Sector --> "*" Course : courses  'opposite: sector
Session --> "*" Participant : registeredParticipants
Session --> Trainer : trainer
Trainer --|> Person
@enduml

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Operation Specifications
Course::cancelSession
Summary: Cancels a session scheduled for a specific date. Deletion is only permitted if the session has zero registered participants.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: Course.sessions, Session.registeredParticipants
Related Classes: Session, Participant, LocalDate
Input: date (LocalDate in "yyyy-MM-dd" format representing the session to cancel)
Output: boolean (true if cancellation succeeds; false if session not found or contains participants)
Pre-condition: 'date' is not null.
Post-condition: If successful, the matching session is removed from Course.sessions and its participant registry is cleared; otherwise, state remains unchanged.

Course::removeDocument
Summary: Deletes a referenced document from the course's document repository.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: Course.documents
Related Classes: Document
Input: doc (Document object to be removed)
Output: boolean (true if removal was attempted/completed; false if 'doc' is null)
Pre-condition: 'doc' is not null.
Post-condition: If 'doc' existed in Course.documents, it is removed; otherwise, state remains unchanged.

Course::addSession
Summary: Schedules a new session for the course on a specific date, enforcing a maximum of one session per course per day. Returns the updated session roster.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: Course.sessions, Session.date
Related Classes: Session, LocalDate, List
Input: date (LocalDate in "yyyy-MM-dd" format representing the scheduled session date)
Output: List<Session> (the up-to-date list of all sessions for the course after the operation)
Pre-condition: 'date' is not null; no existing session for this course shares the same date.
Post-condition: A new Session instance with 'date' is added to Course.sessions; the returned list reflects this addition.

Course::addDocument
Summary: Uploads a referenced document to the course's document repository.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: Course.documents
Related Classes: Document
Input: doc (Document object containing a name; must not be null)
Output: boolean (true on successful upload)
Pre-condition: 'doc' is not null.
Post-condition: 'doc' is appended to Course.documents; the course now references the new document.

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Operation Specifications
Session::replaceTrainer
Summary: Replaces the currently assigned trainer with a new one. Subject to the same temporal constraint as initial assignment.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: Session.date, Session.trainer
Related Classes: Trainer, LocalDate
Input: newTrainer (Trainer object to replace the current one), today (LocalDate representing the current system date)
Output: boolean (true if replacement succeeds; false if input is null or timing constraint violated)
Pre-condition: 'newTrainer' is not null; today is strictly earlier than Session.date.
Post-condition: Session.trainer is updated to 'newTrainer'; previous trainer reference is dereferenced.

Session::registerParticipant
Summary: Enrolls a participant in the session. Guarantees no duplicate enrollments for the same participant.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: Session.registeredParticipants
Related Classes: Participant, Person, LocalDate
Input: p (Participant object to enroll), today (LocalDate representing current date; reserved for potential future scheduling constraints)
Output: boolean (true if enrollment succeeds; false if participant is null or already enrolled)
Pre-condition: 'p' is not null.
Post-condition: 'p' is appended to Session.registeredParticipants; duplicate registration is explicitly prevented.

Session::assignTrainer
Summary: Assigns a trainer to lead the session. Strictly enforces that assignment occurs before the session's start date.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: Session.date, Session.trainer
Related Classes: Trainer, LocalDate
Input: t (Trainer object to assign), today (LocalDate representing the current system date)
Output: boolean (true if assignment succeeds; false if trainer is null or timing constraint violated)
Pre-condition: 't' is not null; today is strictly earlier than Session.date.
Post-condition: Session.trainer references 't'; no other state is modified.

# Operation Specifications
Session::replaceTrainer
Summary: Replaces the currently assigned trainer with a new one. Subject to the same temporal constraint as initial assignment.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: Session.date, Session.trainer
Related Classes: Trainer, LocalDate
Input: newTrainer (Trainer object to replace the current one), today (LocalDate representing the current system date)
Output: boolean (true if replacement succeeds; false if input is null or timing constraint violated)
Pre-condition: 'newTrainer' is not null; today is strictly earlier than Session.date.
Post-condition: Session.trainer is updated to 'newTrainer'; previous trainer reference is dereferenced.

Session::registerParticipant
Summary: Enrolls a participant in the session. Guarantees no duplicate enrollments for the same participant.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: Session.registeredParticipants
Related Classes: Participant, Person, LocalDate
Input: p (Participant object to enroll), today (LocalDate representing current date; reserved for potential future scheduling constraints)
Output: boolean (true if enrollment succeeds; false if participant is null or already enrolled)
Pre-condition: 'p' is not null.
Post-condition: 'p' is appended to Session.registeredParticipants; duplicate registration is explicitly prevented.

Session::assignTrainer
Summary: Assigns a trainer to lead the session. Strictly enforces that assignment occurs before the session's start date.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: Session.date, Session.trainer
Related Classes: Trainer, LocalDate
Input: t (Trainer object to assign), today (LocalDate representing the current system date)
Output: boolean (true if assignment succeeds; false if trainer is null or timing constraint violated)
Pre-condition: 't' is not null; today is strictly earlier than Session.date.
Post-condition: Session.trainer references 't'; no other state is modified.

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Operation Specifications
Course::cancelSession
Summary: Cancels/removes a scheduled session for the course on a specified date.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: sessions, Session.registeredParticipants
Related Classes: Session, Participant
Input: date (LocalDate): Target session date, expected to be derived from "yyyy-MM-dd" format.
Output: boolean: True if successfully cancelled; false otherwise.
Pre-condition: A session exists on the specified date.
Post-condition: If successful, the session is removed from 'sessions' and true is returned. If participants are present, state is unchanged and false is returned.

Course::removeDocument
Summary: Detaches a referenced document from the course.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: documents
Related Classes: Document
Input: doc (Document): The document object to be removed.
Output: boolean: True if successfully removed; false otherwise.
Pre-condition: The Course instance is initialized.
Post-condition: If successful, 'doc' is removed from 'documents' and true is returned. Otherwise, state remains unchanged and false is returned.

Course::addSession
Summary: Schedules a new session for the course on a specified date.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: sessions
Related Classes: Session, LocalDate
Input: date (LocalDate): Target session date, expected to be derived from "yyyy-MM-dd" format.
Output: List<Session>: The complete, up-to-date list of sessions for the course.
Pre-condition: 'date' corresponds to a valid calendar date. No session currently exists for this course on this date.
Post-condition: A new session is added to 'sessions'. The updated list is returned.

Course::addDocument
Summary: Attaches a referenced document to the course.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: documents
Related Classes: Document
Input: doc (Document): The document object to be attached to the course.
Output: boolean: True if successfully added; false if a duplicate already exists.
Pre-condition: The Course instance is initialized. 'doc' is a valid Document object.

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

Course::cancelSession
Summary: Cancels/removes a scheduled session for the course on a specified date.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: sessions, Session.registeredParticipants
Related Classes: Session, Participant

Output: boolean: True if successfully cancelled; false otherwise.
Pre-condition: A session exists on the specified date.
Post-condition: If successful, the session is removed from 'sessions' and true is returned. If participants are present, state is unchanged and false is returned.

Course::removeDocument
Summary: Detaches a referenced document from the course.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: documents
Related Classes: Document
Input: doc (Document): The document object to be removed.
Output: boolean: True if successfully removed; false otherwise.
Pre-condition: The Course instance is initialized.
Post-condition: If successful, 'doc' is removed from 'documents' and true is returned. Otherwise, state remains unchanged and false is returned.

Course::addSession
Summary: Schedules a new session for the course on a specified date.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: sessions
Related Classes: Session, LocalDate
Input: date (LocalDate): Target session date, expected to be derived from "yyyy-MM-dd" format.
Output: List<Session>: The complete, up-to-date list of sessions for the course.
Pre-condition: 'date' corresponds to a valid calendar date. No session currently exists for this course on this date.
Post-condition: A new session is added to 'sessions'. The updated list is returned.

Algorithm: 
Related Features: documents
Related Classes: Document

Pre-condition: The Course instance is initialized. 'doc' is a valid Document object.
Post-condition: If successful, 'doc' is contained in the 'documents' list and true is returned. Otherwise, state remains unchanged and false is returned.

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

5. Input: the input parameters, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
6. Output: output value, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
7. Pre-condition: the condition that the system and the input must satisfy before the operation is executed;
8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

    id : String

}

    id : String
    courses : List<Course>
    addCourse(course : Course) : void
    removeCourse(course : Course) : void
}

    date : LocalDate
    registeredParticipants : List<Participant>
    trainer : Trainer

    replaceTrainer(newTrainer : Trainer, today : LocalDate) : boolean
}

    contractor : boolean
}

Trainer --|> Person
@enduml

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Operation Specifications
Course::addSession
Summary: Schedules a new training session for the course on a specific date, enforcing a maximum of one session per day.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: sessions
Related Classes: Session, LocalDate
Input: date (LocalDate): Target session date in "yyyy-MM-dd" format.
Output: List<Session>: The complete, up-to-date list of sessions for this course.
Pre-condition: date is a valid, non-null date.
Post-condition: A session corresponding to the given date exists in the sessions list. If a session for that date already existed, the list remains unchanged.

Course::cancelSession
Summary: Removes a scheduled session from the course. Cancellation is only permitted if the session has zero registered participants.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: sessions, registeredParticipants
Related Classes: Session, Participant
Input: date (LocalDate): Target session date in "yyyy-MM-dd" format.
Output: boolean: true if the session is successfully removed; false if not found or has participants.
Pre-condition: date is a valid, non-null date.
Post-condition: If successful, the session for the given date is removed from the sessions list. Otherwise, the list remains unchanged.

Course::removeDocument
Summary: Detaches and removes a specific document from the course's document list.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: documents
Related Classes: Document
Input: doc (Document): The document object to be removed.
Output: boolean: true if the document is successfully removed; false otherwise.
Pre-condition: doc is not null.
Post-condition: The document is excluded from the course's documents list.

Course::addDocument
Summary: Adds a document to the course's collection of referenced documents.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: documents
Related Classes: Document
Input: doc (Document): The document object to be attached to the course.
Output: boolean: true if the document is successfully added or already exists; false otherwise.
Pre-condition: doc is not null.
Post-condition: The document is guaranteed to be present in the course's documents list.

# Operation Specifications
Session::assignTrainer
Summary: Assigns a trainer to lead the session, enforcing a strict deadline that assignment cannot occur on or after the session date.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: trainer, date
Related Classes: Trainer, LocalDate
Input: t (Trainer), today (LocalDate): The trainer to assign and the current system date for validation.
Output: boolean: true if assignment succeeds; false if trainer is null or timing constraint violated.
Pre-condition: t is not null. today is strictly earlier than session.date.
Post-condition: The session's trainer field is set to t.

Session::replaceTrainer
Summary: Replaces an existing trainer with a new one, enforcing the same pre-session deadline as initial assignment.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: trainer, date
Related Classes: Trainer, LocalDate
Input: newTrainer (Trainer), today (LocalDate): The replacement trainer and current system date for validation.
Output: boolean: true if replacement succeeds; false if trainer is null or timing constraint violated.
Pre-condition: newTrainer is not null. today is strictly earlier than session.date.
Post-condition: The session's trainer field is updated to newTrainer.

Session::registerParticipant
Summary: Enrolls a participant in the session, preventing duplicate registrations for the same participant.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: registeredParticipants
Related Classes: Participant
Input: p (Participant), today (LocalDate): The participant to enroll and current date (kept for API consistency).
Output: boolean: true if registration succeeds; false if participant is null or already enrolled.
Pre-condition: p is not null.
Post-condition: The participant is added to the session's registeredParticipants list if not already present.

Summary: Assigns a trainer to lead the session, enforcing a strict deadline that assignment cannot occur on or after the session date.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: trainer, date
Related Classes: Trainer, LocalDate
Input: t (Trainer), today (LocalDate): The trainer to assign and the current system date for validation.
Output: boolean: true if assignment succeeds; false if trainer is null or timing constraint violated.
Pre-condition: t is not null. today is strictly earlier than session.date.
Post-condition: The session's trainer field is set to t.

Session::replaceTrainer
Summary: Replaces an existing trainer with a new one, enforcing the same pre-session deadline as initial assignment.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: trainer, date
Related Classes: Trainer, LocalDate
Input: newTrainer (Trainer), today (LocalDate): The replacement trainer and current system date for validation.
Output: boolean: true if replacement succeeds; false if trainer is null or timing constraint violated.
Pre-condition: newTrainer is not null. today is strictly earlier than session.date.
Post-condition: The session's trainer field is updated to newTrainer.

Session::registerParticipant
Summary: Enrolls a participant in the session, preventing duplicate registrations for the same participant.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: registeredParticipants
Related Classes: Participant
Input: p (Participant), today (LocalDate): The participant to enroll and current date (kept for API consistency).
Output: boolean: true if registration succeeds; false if participant is null or already enrolled.
Pre-condition: p is not null.
Post-condition: The participant is added to the session's registeredParticipants list if not already present.

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Operation Specifications
School::addSector
Summary: Creates and registers a new sector within the school organization.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: sectors
Related Classes: Sector, String
Input: id (String): Unique identifier for the new sector.
Output: Sector: The newly created sector instance (or existing one if ID conflicts).
Pre-condition: id is not null or empty.
Post-condition: A new Sector instance with the provided ID is added to the school's sectors collection.

School::assignCourseToSector
Summary: Assigns a course to a target sector, automatically detaching it from any previously assigned sector.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: courses, sectors, sector
Related Classes: Course, Sector, String
Input: courseId (String), sectorId (String): Identifiers for the course and the destination sector.
Output: boolean: true if assignment succeeds; false if either entity is missing.
Pre-condition: Both courseId and sectorId correspond to existing entities in the school.
Post-condition: The course is exclusively linked to the target sector. Any prior sector association is severed.

School::addCourse
Summary: Registers a new course in the school system using a case-sensitive unique identifier.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: courses
Related Classes: Course, String
Input: id (String): Case-sensitive unique identifier for the new course.
Output: boolean: true if the course is successfully registered; false if ID is invalid or duplicate.
Pre-condition: id is not null or empty.
Post-condition: A new Course instance with the provided ID is added to the school's courses collection.

# Operation Specifications
School::addSector
Summary: Creates and registers a new sector within the school organization.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: sectors
Related Classes: Sector, String
Input: id (String): Unique identifier for the new sector.
Output: Sector: The newly created sector instance (or existing one if ID conflicts).
Pre-condition: id is not null or empty.
Post-condition: A new Sector instance with the provided ID is added to the school's sectors collection.

School::assignCourseToSector
Summary: Assigns a course to a target sector, automatically detaching it from any previously assigned sector.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: courses, sectors, sector
Related Classes: Course, Sector, String
Input: courseId (String), sectorId (String): Identifiers for the course and the destination sector.
Output: boolean: true if assignment succeeds; false if either entity is missing.
Pre-condition: Both courseId and sectorId correspond to existing entities in the school.
Post-condition: The course is exclusively linked to the target sector. Any prior sector association is severed.

School::addCourse
Summary: Registers a new course in the school system using a case-sensitive unique identifier.
Algorithm: 
Related Features: courses
Related Classes: Course, String
Input: id (String): Case-sensitive unique identifier for the new course.
Output: boolean: true if the course is successfully registered; false if ID is invalid or duplicate.
Pre-condition: id is not null or empty.
Post-condition: A new Course instance with the provided ID is added to the school's courses collection.

You will be given a **Requirement** and a **Class Diagram** in PlantUML. Your task is to annotate every operation listed in **Operations** with a specification.

An operation specification must describe the following sections about the operation:
1. Summary: the summary of functionality;
2. Algorithm: algorithm or pseudo code;
3. Related Features: a list of structural or behavior features within this class that shall be accessed;
4. Related Classes: a list of classes and data types defined in **Class Diagram** that shall be accessed, in the format of `Related Classes: ClsA, CLsB, ...` or `Related Classes: None`;
5. Input: the input parameters, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
6. Output: output value, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
7. Pre-condition: the condition that the system and the input must satisfy before the operation is executed;
8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

Finish this task by following the guidelines below.
1. Take the principle of modularization into account.
2. For each operation, determine its functional boundary based on the given requirement. Ensure high cohesion and low coupling.
3. If there is any unspecified details, such as undefined constants, rates, and ratios, then you must infer them.

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Operation Specifications
Course::addSession
Summary: Schedules a new session for the course on the specified date, enforcing a maximum of one session per course per day. Returns the updated session list.
Algorithm: 
1. Validate that date is not null and conforms to yyyy-MM-dd format.
2. Scan this.sessions for an existing session with a matching date.
3. If found, return this.sessions immediately (enforce uniqueness).
4. If not found, instantiate a new Session with the provided date.
5. Add the new Session to this.sessions.
6. Return this.sessions.
Related Features: sessions
Related Classes: Session, LocalDate
Input: date (String or LocalDate): Target session date in yyyy-MM-dd format.
Output: List<Session>: The up-to-date list of sessions associated with the course.
Pre-condition: date is valid and not null.
Post-condition: If no session existed for the date, a new Session is created and added to this.sessions. The returned list reflects the current state.

Course::removeDocument
Summary: Deletes a previously uploaded document from the course.
Algorithm: 
1. If doc is null, return false.
2. Check if doc exists in this.documents.
3. If yes, remove it from the list.
4. Return true.
5. If no, return false.
Related Features: documents
Related Classes: Document
Input: doc (Document): The document object to be deleted.
Output: boolean: true if successfully removed, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: doc is not null.
Post-condition: doc is removed from this.documents. Size decreases by 1 if present.

Course::cancelSession
Summary: Cancels a scheduled session for the course on the specified date. Deletion is permitted only if the session has zero registered participants.
Algorithm: 
1. Locate session in this.sessions matching the provided date.
2. If not found, return false.
3. Check session.registeredParticipants.size().
4. If size > 0, return false (enforce participant constraint).
5. Remove session from this.sessions.
6. Clear session's internal references if necessary.
7. Return true.
Related Features: sessions
Related Classes: Session, Participant
Input: date (String or LocalDate): Target session date in yyyy-MM-dd format.
Output: boolean: true if session successfully cancelled, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: date is valid. Session exists for the course on this date.
Post-condition: If successful, the session is removed from this.sessions and its participant list is cleared. System state remains unchanged otherwise.

Course::addDocument
Summary: Uploads a referenced document to the course's document collection.
Algorithm: 
1. If doc is null, return false.
2. If doc already exists in this.documents, return false (prevent duplicates).
3. Append doc to this.documents.
4. Return true.
Related Features: documents
Related Classes: Document
Input: doc (Document): The document object to be uploaded. Must contain a valid name field.
Output: boolean: true if successfully added, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: The Course instance exists. doc is not null.
Post-condition: doc is appended to this.documents. The total count of documents increases by 1.

# Operation Specifications
Course::addSession
Summary: Schedules a new session for the course on the specified date, enforcing a maximum of one session per course per day. Returns the updated session list.
Algorithm: 
1. Validate that date is not null and conforms to yyyy-MM-dd format.
2. Scan this.sessions for an existing session with a matching date.
3. If found, return this.sessions immediately (enforce uniqueness).
4. If not found, instantiate a new Session with the provided date.
5. Add the new Session to this.sessions.
6. Return this.sessions.
Related Features: sessions
Related Classes: Session, LocalDate
Input: date (String or LocalDate): Target session date in yyyy-MM-dd format.
Output: List<Session>: The up-to-date list of sessions associated with the course.
Pre-condition: date is valid and not null.
Post-condition: If no session existed for the date, a new Session is created and added to this.sessions. The returned list reflects the current state.

Course::removeDocument
Summary: Deletes a previously uploaded document from the course.
Algorithm: 
1. If doc is null, return false.
2. Check if doc exists in this.documents.
3. If yes, remove it from the list.
4. Return true.
5. If no, return false.
Related Features: documents
Related Classes: Document
Input: doc (Document): The document object to be deleted.
Output: boolean: true if successfully removed, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: doc is not null.
Post-condition: doc is removed from this.documents. Size decreases by 1 if present.

Course::cancelSession
Summary: Cancels a scheduled session for the course on the specified date. Deletion is permitted only if the session has zero registered participants.
Algorithm: 
1. Locate session in this.sessions matching the provided date.
2. If not found, return false.
3. Check session.registeredParticipants.size().
4. If size > 0, return false (enforce participant constraint).
5. Remove session from this.sessions.
6. Clear session's internal references if necessary.
7. Return true.
Related Features: sessions
Related Classes: Session, Participant
Input: date (String or LocalDate): Target session date in yyyy-MM-dd format.
Output: boolean: true if session successfully cancelled, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: date is valid. Session exists for the course on this date.
Post-condition: If successful, the session is removed from this.sessions and its participant list is cleared. System state remains unchanged otherwise.

Course::addDocument
Summary: Uploads a referenced document to the course's document collection.
Algorithm: 
1. If doc is null, return false.
2. If doc already exists in this.documents, return false (prevent duplicates).
3. Append doc to this.documents.
4. Return true.
Related Features: documents
Related Classes: Document
Input: doc (Document): The document object to be uploaded. Must contain a valid name field.
Output: boolean: true if successfully added, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: The Course instance exists. doc is not null.
Post-condition: doc is appended to this.documents. The total count of documents increases by 1.

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Operation Specifications
Course::addSession
Summary: Schedules a new session for the course on a specific date, ensuring daily uniqueness. Returns the updated session list.
Algorithm:
  VALIDATE date format (yyyy-MM-dd)
  targetSession = SEARCH this.sessions WHERE session.date == date
  IF targetSession IS NOT NULL THEN RETURN null  // Duplicate rejection
  CREATE newSession WITH date = date
  APPEND newSession TO this.sessions
  SORT this.sessions BY date ASC
  RETURN this.sessions
Related Features: sessions, Session.date
Related Classes: Session, LocalDate
Input: date (LocalDate): Target session date in yyyy-MM-dd format.
Output: List<Session>: Updated ordered list of all course sessions on success; null on failure (duplicate date).
Pre-condition: date is a valid LocalDate; not null.
Post-condition: On success, a new session with the given date is added and the list is returned; duplicate dates are rejected without modification.

Course::removeDocument
Summary: Deletes a previously uploaded document from the course's document list.
Algorithm:
  IF doc NOT IN this.documents THEN RETURN false
  REMOVE doc FROM this.documents
  RETURN true
Related Features: documents
Related Classes: Document
Input: doc (Document): The document object to delete.
Output: boolean: true if successfully removed; false if not found.
Pre-condition: doc is not null.
Post-condition: On success, doc is removed from this.documents; otherwise, this.documents remains unchanged.

Course::cancelSession
Summary: Removes a scheduled session, permitted only if the session has zero registered participants.
Algorithm:
  targetSession = SEARCH this.sessions WHERE session.date == date
  IF targetSession IS NULL THEN RETURN false
  IF targetSession.registeredParticipants IS NOT EMPTY THEN RETURN false
  REMOVE targetSession FROM this.sessions
  RETURN true
Related Features: sessions, Session.registeredParticipants
Related Classes: Session, Participant
Input: date (LocalDate): Date of the session to cancel.
Output: boolean: true if successfully canceled; false otherwise.
Pre-condition: date is valid; session exists in this.sessions.
Post-condition: On success, the session is removed from this.sessions; otherwise, this.sessions remains unchanged.

Course::addDocument
Summary: Uploads a document to the course's referenced document list.
Algorithm: 
  IF doc IS NULL OR doc.name IS EMPTY THEN RETURN false
  IF doc IN this.documents THEN RETURN false
  APPEND doc TO this.documents
  RETURN true
Related Features: documents, Document.name
Related Classes: Document
Input: doc (Document): The document object to upload. Contains a name attribute.
Output: boolean: true if successfully added; false if already present or invalid.
Pre-condition: doc is not null; doc.name is not empty.
Post-condition: On success, doc is appended to this.documents; otherwise, this.documents remains unchanged.

# Operation Specifications
School::addCourse
Summary: Registers a new course in the school system using a case-sensitive unique ID.
Algorithm:
  FOR EACH course IN this.courses DO
    IF course.id EQUALS courseId (case-sensitive) THEN RETURN false
  END FOR
  CREATE newCourse WITH id = courseId
  APPEND newCourse TO this.courses
  RETURN true
Related Features: courses, Course.id
Related Classes: Course
Input: id (String): Case-sensitive unique identifier for the new course.
Output: boolean: true if course created and added; false if ID already exists.
Pre-condition: id is not null or blank.
Post-condition: On success, this.courses contains the new course; otherwise, this.courses remains unchanged.

School::assignCourseToSector
Summary: Assigns a course to a target sector, enforcing single-sector membership. Detaches from previous sector if necessary.
Algorithm:
  course = FIND this.courses WHERE course.id == courseId
  targetSector = FIND this.sectors WHERE sector.id == sectorId
  IF course IS NULL OR targetSector IS NULL THEN RETURN false
  IF course.sector IS NOT NULL AND course.sector != targetSector THEN
    course.sector.removeCourse(course)
  END IF
  targetSector.addCourse(course)
  RETURN true
Related Features: courses, sectors, Course.sector, Sector.courses
Related Classes: Course, Sector
Input: courseId (String): ID of the course to assign. sectorId (String): ID of the target sector.
Output: boolean: true if successfully assigned; false if IDs invalid or already correctly assigned.
Pre-condition: courseId and sectorId correspond to existing entities in the school.
Post-condition: The course belongs exclusively to targetSector; its previous sector link is cleared if changed.

School::addSector
Summary: Creates a new sector within the school system.
Algorithm:
  CREATE newSector WITH id = sectorId
  APPEND newSector TO this.sectors
  RETURN newSector
Related Features: sectors, Sector.id
Related Classes: Sector
Input: id (String): Unique identifier for the new sector.
Output: Sector: The newly instantiated sector object.
Pre-condition: id is not null or blank.
Post-condition: this.sectors contains the new sector.
