Post-condition: On success, this.courses contains the new course; otherwise, this.courses remains unchanged.

School::assignCourseToSector
Summary: Assigns a course to a target sector, enforcing single-sector membership. Detaches from previous sector if necessary.
Algorithm:
  course = FIND this.courses WHERE course.id == courseId
  targetSector = FIND this.sectors WHERE sector.id == sectorId
  IF course IS NULL OR targetSector IS NULL THEN RETURN false
  IF course.sector IS NOT NULL AND course.sector != targetSector THEN
    course.sector.removeCourse(course)
  END IF
  targetSector.addCourse(course)
  RETURN true
Related Features: courses, sectors, Course.sector, Sector.courses
Related Classes: Course, Sector
Input: courseId (String): ID of the course to assign. sectorId (String): ID of the target sector.
Output: boolean: true if successfully assigned; false if IDs invalid or already correctly assigned.
Pre-condition: courseId and sectorId correspond to existing entities in the school.
Post-condition: The course belongs exclusively to targetSector; its previous sector link is cleared if changed.

School::addSector
Summary: Creates a new sector within the school system.
Algorithm:
  CREATE newSector WITH id = sectorId
  APPEND newSector TO this.sectors
  RETURN newSector
Related Features: sectors, Sector.id
Related Classes: Sector
Input: id (String): Unique identifier for the new sector.
Output: Sector: The newly instantiated sector object.
Pre-condition: id is not null or blank.
Post-condition: this.sectors contains the new sector.

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Operation Specifications
Session::assignTrainer
Summary: Assigns a trainer to the session, enforcing a strict pre-session deadline.
Algorithm:
  IF today >= this.date THEN RETURN false
  SET this.trainer = t
  RETURN true
Related Features: date, trainer
Related Classes: Trainer, LocalDate
Input: t (Trainer): The trainer to assign. today (LocalDate): Current system date.
Output: boolean: true if assigned successfully; false if deadline violated.
Pre-condition: today is strictly earlier than this.date.
Post-condition: this.trainer is set to t; session state otherwise unchanged.

Session::replaceTrainer
Summary: Replaces the currently assigned trainer for the session, subject to the same strict timing constraint.
Algorithm:
  IF today >= this.date THEN RETURN false
  SET this.trainer = newTrainer
  RETURN true
Related Features: date, trainer
Related Classes: Trainer, LocalDate
Input: newTrainer (Trainer): The replacement trainer. today (LocalDate): Current system date.
Output: boolean: true if replaced successfully; false if deadline violated.
Pre-condition: today is strictly earlier than this.date.
Post-condition: this.trainer is updated to newTrainer; session state otherwise unchanged.

Session::registerParticipant
Summary: Enrolls a participant into the session, preventing duplicate enrollments.
Algorithm:
  IF p IN this.registeredParticipants THEN RETURN false
  APPEND p TO this.registeredParticipants
  RETURN true
Related Features: registeredParticipants
Related Classes: Participant
Input: p (Participant): The participant to register. today (LocalDate): Current system date (passed per signature, reserved for potential future validation).
Output: boolean: true if registered; false if duplicate enrollment.
Pre-condition: p is not null; session instance is valid.
Post-condition: On success, p is added to this.registeredParticipants; otherwise, this.registeredParticipants remains unchanged.

# Operation Specifications
Session::assignTrainer
Summary: Assigns a trainer to the session, enforcing a strict pre-session deadline.
Algorithm:
  IF today >= this.date THEN RETURN false
  SET this.trainer = t
  RETURN true
Related Features: date, trainer
Related Classes: Trainer, LocalDate
Input: t (Trainer): The trainer to assign. today (LocalDate): Current system date.
Output: boolean: true if assigned successfully; false if deadline violated.
Pre-condition: today is strictly earlier than this.date.
Post-condition: this.trainer is set to t; session state otherwise unchanged.

Session::replaceTrainer
Summary: Replaces the currently assigned trainer for the session, subject to the same strict timing constraint.
Algorithm:
  IF today >= this.date THEN RETURN false
  SET this.trainer = newTrainer
  RETURN true
Related Features: date, trainer
Related Classes: Trainer, LocalDate
Input: newTrainer (Trainer): The replacement trainer. today (LocalDate): Current system date.
Output: boolean: true if replaced successfully; false if deadline violated.
Pre-condition: today is strictly earlier than this.date.
Post-condition: this.trainer is updated to newTrainer; session state otherwise unchanged.

Session::registerParticipant
Summary: Enrolls a participant into the session, preventing duplicate enrollments.
Algorithm:
  IF p IN this.registeredParticipants THEN RETURN false
  APPEND p TO this.registeredParticipants
  RETURN true
Related Features: registeredParticipants
Related Classes: Participant
Input: p (Participant): The participant to register. today (LocalDate): Current system date (passed per signature, reserved for potential future validation).
Output: boolean: true if registered; false if duplicate enrollment.
Pre-condition: p is not null; session instance is valid.
Post-condition: On success, p is added to this.registeredParticipants; otherwise, this.registeredParticipants remains unchanged.

    for (Sector s : getSectors()) {

    if (oldSector != null) {

8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

}

    removeCourse(course : Course) : void
}

    date : LocalDate

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Operation Specifications
Session::assignTrainer
Summary: Assigns a designated trainer to lead the session.
Algorithm: 
  1. Compare today with this.date.
  2. If today >= this.date, return false.
  3. Set this.trainer = t.
  4. Return true.
Related Features: Session.date, Session.trainer
Related Classes: Trainer, Session
Input: t (Trainer): The trainer to assign. today (LocalDate): Current system date.
Output: boolean: true if assignment succeeds; false if timing constraint violated.
Pre-condition: today is strictly earlier than this.date; t is not null.
Post-condition: Session.trainer is set to t.

Session::replaceTrainer
Summary: Substitutes the current trainer of the session with a new trainer.
Algorithm: 
  1. Compare today with this.date.
  2. If today >= this.date, return false.
  3. Set this.trainer = newTrainer.
  4. Return true.
Related Features: Session.date, Session.trainer
Related Classes: Trainer, Session
Input: newTrainer (Trainer): The replacement trainer. today (LocalDate): Current system date.
Output: boolean: true if replacement succeeds; false if timing constraint violated.
Pre-condition: today is strictly earlier than this.date; newTrainer is not null.
Post-condition: Session.trainer is updated to newTrainer.

Session::registerParticipant
Summary: Enrolls a participant into the session, preventing duplicate registrations.
Algorithm:

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Operation Specifications
Session::assignTrainer
Summary: Assigns a designated trainer to lead the session.
Algorithm: 
  1. Compare today with this.date.
  2. If today >= this.date, return false.
  3. Set this.trainer = t.
  4. Return true.
Related Features: Session.date, Session.trainer
Related Classes: Trainer, Session
Input: t (Trainer): The trainer to assign. today (LocalDate): Current system date.
Output: boolean: true if assignment succeeds; false if timing constraint violated.
Pre-condition: today is strictly earlier than this.date; t is not null.
Post-condition: Session.trainer is set to t.

Session::replaceTrainer
Summary: Substitutes the current trainer of the session with a new trainer.
Algorithm: 
  1. Compare today with this.date.
  2. If today >= this.date, return false.
  3. Set this.trainer = newTrainer.
  4. Return true.
Related Features: Session.date, Session.trainer
Related Classes: Trainer, Session
Input: newTrainer (Trainer): The replacement trainer. today (LocalDate): Current system date.
Output: boolean: true if replacement succeeds; false if timing constraint violated.
Pre-condition: today is strictly earlier than this.date; newTrainer is not null.
Post-condition: Session.trainer is updated to newTrainer.

Session::registerParticipant
Summary: Enrolls a participant into the session, preventing duplicate registrations.
Algorithm: 
  1. Check if p is already contained in this.registeredParticipants.
  2. If yes, return false.
  3. Add p to this.registeredParticipants.
  4. Return true.
Related Features: Session.registeredParticipants
Related Classes: Participant, Session
Input: p (Participant): The participant to enroll. today (LocalDate): Current date (accepted per signature; primary logic enforces deduplication per functional requirement).
Output: boolean: true if successfully registered; false if already enrolled.
Pre-condition: p is not null.
Post-condition: If true, p is added to Session.registeredParticipants. If false, list remains unchanged.

# Operation Specifications
Course::addSession
Summary: Schedules a new training session for the course on a specified date.
Algorithm: 
  1. Search this.sessions for an existing session where session.date equals date.
  2. If found, return the current this.sessions list.
  3. If not found, create a new Session instance with date, add it to this.sessions, and return the updated this.sessions list.
Related Features: Course.sessions
Related Classes: Session, Course
Input: date (LocalDate): Target session date in yyyy-MM-dd format.
Output: List<Session>: The complete, up-to-date list of sessions for the course.
Pre-condition: date is a valid date; no session exists for the course on this date.
Post-condition: If new, a session is added to Course.sessions. If duplicate, list remains identical.

Course::addDocument
Summary: Uploads a referenced document to the course catalog.
Algorithm: 
  1. Append doc to this.documents.
  2. Return true.
Related Features: Course.documents
Related Classes: Document, Course
Input: doc (Document): The document object to upload.
Output: boolean: true on success.
Pre-condition: doc is not null.
Post-condition: doc is included in Course.documents.

Course::cancelSession
Summary: Cancels an existing training session for the course, enforcing a no-participants rule.
Algorithm: 
  1. Locate session by date in this.sessions.
  2. If not found, return false.
  3. If session.registeredParticipants.size() > 0, return false.
  4. Remove session from this.sessions.
  5. Return true.
Related Features: Course.sessions
Related Classes: Session, Course
Input: date (LocalDate): Date of the session to cancel in yyyy-MM-dd format.
Output: boolean: true if successfully canceled; false if session not found or has participants.
Pre-condition: Session exists for the given date.
Post-condition: If true, session is removed from Course.sessions and had zero participants beforehand. If false, system state is unchanged.

Course::removeDocument
Summary: Deletes a referenced document from the course catalog.
Algorithm: 
  1. Attempt to remove doc from this.documents.
  2. Return true if removal succeeded, otherwise false.
Related Features: Course.documents
Related Classes: Document, Course
Input: doc (Document): The document object to delete.
Output: boolean: true if successfully deleted; false if document was not found.
Pre-condition: doc is not null.
Post-condition: If true, doc is removed from Course.documents. State unchanged if false.

# Operation Specifications
School::addSector
Summary: Creates and registers a new sector within the school.
Algorithm: 
  1. Instantiate a new Sector object using id.
  2. Append the new sector to this.sectors.
  3. Return the new sector object.
Related Features: School.sectors
Related Classes: Sector
Input: id (String): Unique identifier for the sector.
Output: Sector: The newly created sector instance.
Pre-condition: id is valid (non-null).
Post-condition: The new sector is included in School.sectors.

School::addCourse
Summary: Adds a new course to the school with a specified unique ID.
Algorithm: 
  1. Iterate through this.courses to check if any existing course has an id equal to id.
  2. If a match is found, return false.
  3. Otherwise, instantiate a new Course object with id, append it to this.courses, and return true.
Related Features: School.courses
Related Classes: Course
Input: id (String): Case-sensitive unique identifier for the course. Non-empty string.
Output: boolean: true if the course was successfully added; false if a course with the same ID already exists.
Pre-condition: The system is initialized; id is not null or empty.
Post-condition: If true, a new Course instance with the given id is appended to School.courses. If false, the school's state remains unchanged.

School::assignCourseToSector
Summary: Assigns a course to a specific sector, automatically detaching it from any previous sector if applicable.
Algorithm: 
  1. Locate the Course object matching courseId in this.courses.
  2. Locate the Sector object matching sectorId in this.sectors.
  3. If either entity is not found, return false.
  4. If the course currently has a sector (not null), call course.sector.removeCourse(course).
  5. Call targetSector.addCourse(course).
  6. Return true.
Related Features: School.courses, School.sectors, Course.sector, Sector.courses
Related Classes: Course, Sector
Input: courseId (String): ID of the course to assign. sectorId (String): ID of the target sector.
Output: boolean: true if assignment succeeds; false if course or sector not found.
Pre-condition: Both courseId and sectorId correspond to existing entities in the school.
Post-condition: The course's sector attribute points to the target sector. The target sector's courses list contains the course. If previously assigned elsewhere, it is removed from there.

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```
